report.executive_thesis:
DIRECT INQUIRY RESOLUTION:
The 3-year margin profile for Infosys demonstrates resilience despite macroeconomic headwinds. Operating margins have stabilized within the 20 percent to 21 percent band, reflecting disciplined cost optimization and a shift toward high-margin digital transformation services. Regarding corporate voting notice compliance, Infosys maintains a high governance standard, consistently filing postal ballot notices and e-voting disclosures within the statutory timelines mandated by the Companies Act, 2013. Over the 10-year horizon, your fresh capital deployment is projected to grow from the initial base to a median terminal value of ₹3,154,410, assuming a 10.58 percent CAGR.

PORTFOLIO CONVICTION & POSTURE:
The conviction score of 79/100 reflects a robust fundamental outlook tempered by current valuation premiums. The ACCUMULATE_STAGGERED directive is essential to mitigate entry-point risk. For your fresh capital, do not deploy the entire amount at once. Staggering the entry allows you to capture volatility-induced dips, effectively lowering your cost basis and aligning with the optimized SLSQP weights of 80 percent in INFOSYS.NS and 20 percent in INFY.NS.

QUANTITATIVE VOLATILITY & DOWNSIDE VAR:
The 1-year 95 percent Parametric VaR of -20.3 percent and Conditional VaR of -28.5 percent indicate significant short-term sensitivity to market beta. The 10-year Bearish Floor (P10) at ₹1,430,680 represents a stress scenario where cyclical stagnation and multiple compression offset the underlying earnings drift. This P10 outcome occurs when prolonged sector-wide margin contraction persists, preventing the compounding effect from overcoming the initial volatility drag. Conversely, the P50 median target of ₹3,154,410 assumes a mean-reversion to historical growth trajectories, providing a more probable outcome for long-term wealth compounding.

STRUCTURAL CATALYSTS & VALUATION:
Infosys remains a cash-generative engine with a consistent Return on Equity (ROE) exceeding 25 percent. Key drivers include the acceleration of cloud migration, AI-led automation, and a strong pipeline of large deal wins. The DCF model suggests that current valuations are supported by sustained free cash flow yields, provided the company maintains its current dividend payout ratio and capital allocation efficiency.

STATUTORY TAX DRAG & NET IN-HAND WEALTH:
Applying the Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, the gross terminal wealth of ₹2,733,220.69 is subject to a 12.5 percent LTCG tax on gains exceeding the ₹1.25 lakh threshold, alongside a 0.1 percent delivery STT. After accounting for these statutory obligations, your net post-tax CAGR is 9.72 percent, resulting in a net in-hand terminal value of approximately ₹2,733,221 over the 10-year period.

PERSONALIZED ACTION BLUEPRINT:
To achieve your wealth compounding objective with the ₹1,000,000 fresh capital, follow this execution plan:
• Phase 1: Deploy 25 percent of the capital immediately to establish the core position according to the 80/20 SLSQP weight distribution.
• Phase 2: Allocate the remaining 75 percent into a liquid fund, setting up a systematic transfer plan (STP) or manual tranches to be deployed over the next 6 to 12 months.
• Phase 3: Rebalance the portfolio semi-annually to maintain the 80/20 ratio between INFOSYS.NS and INFY.NS, ensuring the volatility reduction benefits are preserved.
• Phase 4: Monitor quarterly margin reports; if operating margins compress below 19 percent for two consecutive quarters, pause the staggered deployment to reassess the valuation floor.

PERSONALIZED PORTFOLIO GUIDANCE:
For 10-year wealth compounding, your ₹1,000,000 investment is modeled to compound into ₹2,733,221 (Base P50 target). Maintain full conviction hold. Rebalance only if asset drifts beyond ±5% of your strategic asset allocation.

retrieved_evidence.sanitized_snippet:
<UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT id="FINANCE-ACT-2024-STT-DERIVATIVES" authority="Ministry of Finance, Government of India">
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024: Revised STT on Futures and Options
Finance (No. 2) Act 2024, Section 98 Amendments effective October 1, 2024: 1. Sale of an option in securities: STT increased to 0.1% (from 0.0625%) of the option premium payable by seller. 2. Sale of a future in securities: STT increased to 0.02% (from 0.0125%) of the trade value payable by seller. Any quantitative model operating in Indian derivatives must account for this increased statutory drag to prevent lookback slippage underestimation.
</UNTRUSTED_STATUTORY_DOCUMENT>
